summary.headline: IRCON Q2 FY27 consol operating revenue INR 2,272 crore and PAT INR 100 crore; H1 order inflow only about INR 1,000 crore against INR 21,296 crore order book.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated total revenue of INR 2,364 crore, operating revenue of INR 2,272 crore, core EBITDA of INR 227 crore and PAT of INR 100 crore, with EPS of INR 1.09. Order book stood at INR 21,296 crore at 30 September 2026, 91% domestic and 55% competitively won. Order inflow has been thin: H1 inflow is about INR 1,000 crore, most of it after 30 September, while management guides to INR 9,000-10,000 crore of orders for the full year. Management guided standalone FY27 operating turnover of INR 9,000-9,500 crore (later INR 9,500-10,000 crore) and held standalone PAT margin of 6-7% and consol core EBITDA margin of 8-9%.

financial_highlights.metric: EPS (Q2, not annualised, face value INR 2)

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore up to 30 Sep, rest after quarter-end

financial_highlights.metric: Effective tax rate Q2 and H1
financial_highlights.change: Includes one-off Sri Lanka tax liability of INR 12-13 crore

financial_highlights.value: About INR 3,100 crore invested; INR 800-900 crore further expected

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Management calls railways the first preference and largest market; about INR 25,000 crore of railway and highway bids are quoted and awaiting opening. Named execution projects include the T-2 bullet train track package (INR 3,000-3,500 crore pending).

segments.name: Highways and HAM / PPP
segments.commentary: Sivok project (West Bengal and Sikkim, tunnels and bridges) has INR 2,000-2,500 crore pending. HAM projects are mostly under construction and expected to complete by end FY27, when dividend income from them should start.

segments.name: Coal connectivity JVs
segments.commentary: Seven JVs, mainly coal connectivity. CERL is the only operational one and is loss-making due to teething issues with coal supply from mines. Breakeven is expected in about two years, with losses reducing next year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: About 9% of order book is international; target is 15%. Focus on Algeria, Sri Lanka, African countries and Eastern Europe, with management citing better margins and less competition.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone operating turnover of INR 9,000-9,500 crore per the earlier call; later stated as INR 9,500-10,000 crore, about 5-6% growth.
FY27 new order target of INR 9,000-10,000 crore, aiming to keep order book at about INR 25,000 crore by March 2027.
Standalone PAT margin guidance of 6-7% maintained; consol core EBITDA margin of 8-9% maintained.
Full-year effective tax rate guided at 23-24%, with the Q2 one-off normalising over the year.
FY28 revenue expected to rise marginally; management will firm up the view a few months later (after February 2027).
capex_capacity: About INR 3,100 crore invested in subsidiaries and JVs; another INR 800-900 crore to be put into assets under construction.
HAM projects under construction, expected to complete by end FY27.
Surplus cash being moved into PPP and HAM equity, which reduces treasury interest income in other income.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 21,296 crore at 30 Sep 2026: 55% competitive, 45% nomination; 91% domestic, 9% international.
H1 inflow about INR 1,000 crore, with a substantial part after 30 September. Order book was about INR 25,000 crore at 31 March 2026, so it has declined.
Management says competition is high, especially in railways, but expects some easing.
Overseas tenders in Algeria, African countries and Eastern Europe, and Sri Lanka, are being bid for.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall on consol and standalone basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the end of ISTPL PPP dividends after its concession ended, a gap before new HAM projects pay dividends, lower interest on surplus cash moved into equity, and smaller exchange gains. It called this a timing difference.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a working capital loan used when cash is high?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about INR 100 crore was drawn last year for projects with large working capital needs. Management says it now uses its own cash and bank balances.

qa_highlights.question: When will JVs turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: CERL is the only operational coal JV and is loss-making; losses should reduce next year and breakeven is expected in about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate about 33% and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-off tax liability of INR 12-13 crore on the completed Sri Lanka project. Management guides a full-year rate of 23-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why does implied order inflow look like only about INR 200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no cancellations; the increase in the order book to 30 September was about INR 200 crore, and inflow to date is about INR 1,000 crore after quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 revenue and the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is conservative: FY27 turnover similar to last year, FY28 revenue to rise marginally, with a clearer view expected after February.

risks_watch: Order inflow is weak: H1 about INR 1,000 crore against a FY27 target of INR 9,000-10,000 crore, and the order book has fallen from about INR 25,000 crore to INR 21,296 crore.
Coal connectivity JVs remain loss-making with breakeven about two years away.
Other income is falling as surplus cash goes into PPP/HAM equity and PPP dividends end.
Management declined to give a firm FY28 view, which raises uncertainty on growth beyond FY27.
Management said it had no knowledge of any RVNL merger, but this question was asked and left open.
Tax rate guidance of 23-24% depends on normalisation of the one-off in later quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the pipeline and targets, but cautious on FY28. Management repeatedly says the market is volatile and uncertain. Answers on order targets were vague, with several repeated figures, and the order-book and order-inflow questions were answered only partly.
key_quotes: We are hopeful that in the next quarter, we will get definitely some good works.
We do think that our revenue will be in the range of INR 9,500 crore-INR 10,000 crore for this year.
It is a very, very large-sized market for us.
As of now, I mean, to probably give you a better feedback on FY 2028 may be few months down the line, because it's a very volatile and a very sensitive market.

growth.why: Management guides standalone FY27 operating turnover of INR 9,500-10,000 crore (about 5-6% growth) backed by a INR 21,296 crore order book (about 2x annual revenue), but H1 order inflow of only about INR 1,000 crore against a FY27 order target of INR 9,000-10,000 crore leaves the order-to-revenue link only partially evidenced, and no new capacity additions are being built.
